issues: (1) No integrity problems. The diff only adds a CrossAttention module to each block, initializes its weights and passes x0 into the blocks. The evaluation call, data, seed lines, the prepare.py import and the final summary printing are not touched.

(2) No bug that makes the result meaningless. The cross-attention uses causal=True with the same window_size, and its keys and values come from x0 (the token embeddings at the same positions), so it cannot see future tokens. RoPE and QK-norm are applied the same way as in self-attention, and c_proj starts at zero, so the model starts out matching the incumbent. One thing I could not check: whether the optimizer setup picks up the new xattn weights. That depends on code outside the diff. If it collects matrix parameters from transformer.h, they are included.

(3) No claims were made beyond the harness numbers. The candidate scored 1.1011 against the incumbent's 1.0943, which is 0.0068 worse (lower val_bpb is better). That fits with each layer doing about 33% more attention work, so fewer steps fit in the fixed 300 s. Rejecting is consistent with the numbers.

z cannot be recomputed on its own: each side has only one run, so there is no variance estimate to divide by. The harness's z = -0.880 implies a noise sigma of about 0.0077 (0.0068 / 0.88). Its sign and size are plausible, but I could not verify the value.
Simplicity: about 25 extra lines and roughly 4·n_embd² more parameters per layer, with no gain. Even if the result were equal, this would not be worth keeping.
